# T7n — National signal: RTFP vs BBS food CPI, and published vs survey (Task 4.3)

*Generated by `analysis/notes.py` from `outputs/tables/T7n_bbs_national.csv and T7n_published_vs_survey_national.csv` (script `analysis/f7_bbs_national.py`).*

**Claim 1 (negative result).** BBS national food CPI cannot validate RTFP's national signal: monthly and 3-month changes of the four-staple RTFP index show no positive association with BBS food inflation (correlation -0.14–0.07 over the BBS overlap, 2014-12 to 2026-09, within-base changes; -0.26–-0.08 from 2020-08), and neither does the survey-only index (correlations -0.26–-0.03 across all periods and horizons). No slope is significant at the 5% level (largest |slope / HAC SE| 1.79). Imputation is therefore not the cause. The basket difference (four staples vs the full food basket) is a plausible explanation, as are timing, coverage or BBS method differences; none is tested here.

**Claim 2.** RTFP's published national index tracks the survey-only national index: monthly log-change correlation 0.81–0.87, slope 0.94–1.19. This is not a real-time test: both indices come from the latest release, whose earlier months may have been revised with survey values that arrived later.

| 2007-2019 | 151 | 0.869 | 0.944 | 0.046 | 0.024 | 0.026 |

**Caveats.** Claim 2 is partly mechanical: observed cells enter both indices. BBS month alignment verified against the official workbook; no splice across the April 2023 rebasing (changes computed within one base). Methodology D4 expected agreement with BBS; that expectation was wrong and is recorded as such.
